summary: This work proposes using fluxonium superconducting circuits to implement qutrit quantum simulators with tunable parameters via external flux bias, identifying four distinct operational regimes characterized by plasmon-like versus fluxon-like excitations. The platform realizes an extended Bose-Hubbard model with three-body hard-core constraint, correlated single-particle and pair hopping, and non-local interactions, exhibiting rich phase diagrams including superfluid, pair-superfluid, Mott-insulator, and pair-checkerboard phases.
motivation: Qutrit-based simulators promise advantages over qubit platforms for exploring strongly correlated bosonic matter and lattice gauge theories, but previous proposals lacked comprehensive treatment of all interaction terms and operational flexibility. Fluxonium circuits offer superior tuning capabilities compared to transmons due to their larger anharmonicity and protection from charge noise.
method: The authors map the coupled fluxonium circuit Hamiltonian to a bosonic qutrit array Hamiltonian using rotating-wave approximation and perturbation theory, analyze four regimes (ΠΠ, ΦΦ, ΠΦ, ΦΠ) achievable with $E_C = 2π × 0.60$ GHz and $E_L = 2π × 1.50$ GHz by tuning $E_J$ and external flux $Φ$, study ground-state phases via Gutzwiller approximation and exact diagonalization, and propose dynamical experiments probing different regimes.
result: Achievable transition frequencies range from $2π × 2.08$ GHz to $2π × 6.06$ GHz with detunings $δ > 2π × 350$ MHz, pair-hopping ratios $P/J$ spanning $0.29$ to $131$, and coherence times $T_φ ≳ 3$ μs limited primarily by flux noise; the phase diagram includes superfluid, pair-superfluid with stiffness $∝ α^2 J^2/|Δ|$, Mott-insulator, and pair-checkerboard phases, with dynamical signatures distinguishable on microsecond timescales.
